Users should be aware of the current technical limitations of AI, including but not limited to: generation of inaccurate or fabricated information, lack of source transparency
reproduction of unintended and potentially harmful biases embedded in training data
use of AI platforms may raise ethical and legal concerns including violations of intellectual property rights
especially when personal or unpublished work is input into these systems that, in turn, may become output to another user.

use of most external AI tools for rephrasing students’ own material to avoid selfplagiarism entails the risk of student's own work being used to train future generations of AI services; while the rephrased output may be based on assessments submitted to another institution - therefore this practice should be avoided.
Submit for assessment only work that they produced themselves and which duly acknowledges ideas, words and works of others that were used in the production of their own work

The failure of the student to attend the meeting will not prevent the Academic Integrity Panel from deciding on the matter and taking appropriate action in accordance with this procedure
It is not required to prove intention for academic misconduct to be confirmed as having taken place.
Termination of studies and no award possible.

In determining the severity of an act of academic misconduct and the penalty to apply, the Academic Integrity Panel will be guided by matters such as the nature of the conduct, the level and year of study, the extent of the academic misconduct and the impact of penalties on the student.

The purpose of the Academic Misconduct Procedure is not solely punitive, in that opportunities should be taken to facilitate a student learning from the experience so that it minimises the likelihood of repetition in the future.

The student has the right to be accompanied at the meeting by one member of the University of Stirling community who is one of the following: fellow student, staff member, or a representative from the University of Stirling Students’ Union.
